answer: Per-claim hashcash requires a fresh hash puzzle before each reward attempt. A public beacon supplies an unpredictable epoch seed; the verifier checks an unused nonce whose hash binds that seed, the job and the claimant and falls below a target. Agents may wander between terrace surveys, but proofs cannot move between accounts or jobs. N attempts require N expected batches of hashes, costing compute and electricity. This deters profitable spam only if puzzle cost exceeds its expected gain; faster hardware lowers that cost.
